title: "An Algebraic Invariance Condition for the Existence of Latent Correlations in Confirmatory Factor Analysis"
shorttitle: "Invariance and Latent-Correlation Existence"

abstract: | 
  An independent cluster model in confirmatory factor analysis (ICM-CFA) assigns each variable to one and only one factor. Variables loading on the same factor form a cluster representing a construct, and correlations among factors represent latent correlations among these constructs. We derive the covariance condition required for a population latent correlation to exist between two clusters. The within- and between-cluster covariance patterns must align up to a common scalar. Each admissible quadruple identifies an alignment ratio, and under ICM-CFA all alignment ratios equal the squared latent correlation. When they differ, no single population latent correlation exists, and fitting ICM-CFA returns a criterion-dependent summary rather than an estimate of a common population quantity. With more than two clusters, this condition applies pairwise. We investigate two forms of misspecification: misassignment, when variables are assigned to the wrong cluster, and misalignment, when correctly assigned covariance patterns do not align. Alignment ratios diagnose both forms of misspecification without additional model fitting, and their invariance condition clarifies the relationship between ICM-CFA and bifactor models.


keywords: |
